key_insight: AgentSSL frames semi-supervised learning as a program search problem, exploring whether automated machine learning engineering agents can use abundant unlabeled data alongside scarce labeled examples. The provided abstract is truncated, so it does not establish performance gains.
problem_solved: Developing ML systems for new domains requires costly labeled data and manual pipeline engineering. Existing MLE agents have been studied mainly in fully supervised settings, leaving their ability to exploit unlabeled data largely untested.
method: Introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL) for settings with limited labeled data and abundant unlabeled data.
Frame semi-supervised pipeline development as a program search problem.
Investigate whether MLE agents can leverage unlabeled data; implementation and evaluation details are unavailable in the provided excerpt.
impact: This work targets a practical gap in automated ML: building pipelines when labels are scarce. If effective, the approach could reduce reliance on annotation and manual engineering, but the excerpt provides no results confirming those benefits.
visual_elements: Two data pools: a small labeled set and a large unlabeled set feeding an MLE agent.
Program search diagram showing an agent exploring candidate semi-supervised pipelines.
Side-by-side workflow illustration contrasting fully supervised automation with AgentSSL.
Bottleneck icons representing annotation cost and manual pipeline engineering.
paper_title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
paper_authors: Ethan Lin, Akanksha Sarkar, Ziang Liu, Kristin Branson, Jennifer J. Sun
